reports.title: Kodiak Sciences Announces Recent Business Highlights and Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

desk.headline: Net loss of $1.05 a share, a little wider than estimates; cash down to $88.7m before raising $69m, with KSI-101 data due in December
results: No revenue yet; net loss widened to $66.2m from $61.5m, but loss per share narrowed to $1.05 from $1.16 because there are more shares.
R&D spending rose to $58.3m from $50.5m on Phase 3 trials and manufacturing; admin costs fell to $8.8m, helped by a one-off lease gain.
Cash fell to $88.7m from $209.9m at the start of the year; after the quarter Kodiak sold shares for $69m net.
Zenkuda and tabirafusp-ted both met the main goal of the Phase 3 DAYBREAK study in wet AMD.

guidance.summary: No financial guidance. Kodiak says current cash supports planned operations into 2027, and its filing flags substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern.

points: CEO Victor Perlroth pitched the company as having three late-stage eye-disease drugs.
First Phase 3 results for KSI-101 (eye swelling from inflammation) are expected in December; if positive, a filing for approval is planned for Q2 2027.
A filing for approval of Zenkuda across three uses, backed by five successful Phase 3 studies, is on track for year end.
Enrolment of the second 600-patient KSI-101 group should finish in Q4, with data in Q2 2027.
call.source: No call coverage found; points from CEO comments in the press release (8-K Exhibit 99.1)

watch: December topline results from the KSI-101 PEAK study.
Whether the Zenkuda approval filing goes in by year end as planned.
Funding: cash runway only into 2027 and the going-concern warning.
